# Week 4 Cone challenge rematch

> [Download the Word version](W04_cone_rematch_Speaker_Notes.docx) · This Markdown copy is generated from the DOCX. Update the DOCX, then run `python scripts/sync_documents.py --write` from the repository root. Print layout, page breaks, headers/footers, and writing-space height remain in Word.

Speaker notes for the one-hour class. Prepare both kits and the printed fields before students arrive.

### Class setup

**Goal**  Each team gets one cone upright into its matching home and can explain a change. A second cone adds a diagonal approach. A third is a stretch.

**Print**  For each of two lanes, print W04\_Cone\_Rematch\_Full\_Size\_Field.pdf pages 2–10 on portrait US Letter at 100%. Page 1 is the assembly guide. Check the 5 cm ruler, trim all four edges, lay out A–B–C / D–E–F / G–H–I, match paired ticks and tape from behind. Tape the field flat. Print W04\_Cone\_Rematch.pdf page 2 once per team plus one spare.

**Rehearse**  Use two 60 × 60 cm fields plus clear floor around each. Start with about 20 cm extra on all sides and increase it if needed. Open W04\_cone\_rematch.py on both kits (A left, B right, SPEED = 200). Fit the low rounded center tip. Dry-run the full course, then test one cone before adding the others. Confirm release and clearance. Starter marks and values are examples, so adjust the baseline or use tape marks that fit each robot before class.

**Set up stations**  Two robot stations and two build tables for T1–T4. Bring six matching 4 cm base cones and spares, two mentor pushers, four build packs or team pushers, four mounting proxies, rulers and tape. Save a baseline and a separate project for each team.

## Slide 1 Cone challenge rematch

**Timing**  0–5 minutes

**Open**  Ask students to show with their hands what happened on one Week 3 trial. Collect one observation such as a tipped cone, a short push or a turn that missed the next cone.

**Mission**  Start with Cone 1 alone. After the final turn, its whole base must be inside Home 1 and the cone must still stand upright. A clean one-cone run is a complete first result. Add cones only after that works.

## Slide 2 Set up the cone field

**Timing**  5–10 minutes

**Show**  Point out the assembled field, the axle start on tile G and the cone and home marks. Center the drive axle on START and make the base face up the arrow. Set only Cone 1 on its dashed circle.

**Demo**  Run the rehearsed project with the mentor pusher. Watch the centered tip push the cone into its home and swing away on the turn. Walk a finger from the first pivot toward Cone 2 to show the diagonal. The cone is in front of the robot on that leg.

**Field reference**  W04\_Cone\_Rematch\_Full\_Size\_Field.pdf pages 2–10 are tiles A through I. Show where the registration ticks meet. Reference the pusher tip sketch on page 2 of W03\_Dance\_Three\_Cone\_Field.pdf if children need help with release.

## Slide 3 Tune one number

**Timing**  10–14 minutes

**Trace**  Use the full W04\_cone\_rematch.py project. Each row gives one forward move and the turn that follows it, both in wheel degrees. Read row 1 aloud and point to the same two calls inside the loop. D is outside the loop and appears once.

**Ask**  If the robot stops short of Home 1, which number could you raise? If it points past Cone 2, which turn already happened? Listen for the drive in row 1 and the turn in row 1, respectively.

**Coach**  Values on screen are a starting example. Use the rehearsed numbers for each kit. The turn value controls wheel rotation. Watch the actual heading. Have the team predict the effect of a small change, such as 10 wheel degrees, before running.

## Slide 4 Try one cone at a time

**Timing**  14–26 and 26–38 minutes

**Rotate**  T1/T3 start on robots and T2/T4 at the build tables, then swap. Robot roles are driver, navigator and observer. Build roles are builder, parts manager and tester. Rotate every four minutes.

**Robot team**  Start with the rehearsed pusher. Align the stopped robot and place Cone 1 on its mark. Run the baseline and ask the observer to write down the first miss or the successful release.

**Build team**  Use the proxy to fit a low centered tip. Hand-push a cone and check that the beam clears it as the base turns. Check that the base of the cone sits flat. Have a mentor approve each attachment before mounting it to a stopped robot.

## Slide 5 Change one thing and retest

**Timing**  38–44 minutes T1/T3, then 44–50 minutes T2/T4

**Test**  Keep the marked start, field, speed and cone placement fixed. Use either one code change or one pusher change. Rotate jobs every two minutes and have each child predict or explain an effect.

**Score**  After the final turn, count upright cones whose whole base is inside the corresponding home. Add Cone 2 after a clean one-cone test. Add Cone 3 if the second run clears the earlier home. If the full route is unreliable, stay with one cone and explain the result.

## Slide 6 Show what your test taught you

**Timing**  50–54 reflection and 54–60 save and reset

**Ask**  Have each child name one observation, prediction or reason for a code or build change. A failed test can still show whether the miss came from aim, distance or the pusher.

**Close**  Save the tested team project and record the actual score and the single change on the team card. Pack the pushers and cones. Preview that in Week 5 the robot will use a reading to decide when to stop.
